facts.claim: eSafety Commissioner, 'Consent for sharing photos and videos' (read 23 November 2026, a page in its Young people section): 'You should always ask for consent before sharing a photo or video.'

facts.claim: eSafety (same page): 'If you're planning to share any images or videos online, it's best to make sure the person or people in the photos or videos are okay with it too.' insider_details.detail: Tell guests that a public post with your tag appears on the tag's page for anyone to see, while posts from private profiles won't show there publicly. Couples who want a quieter gallery should say so on the invitation or welcome note rather than rely on the tag.
Build the tag from letters and numbers only (a wedding year works); spaces and symbols such as $ or % break it on Instagram, so test the exact spelling before it goes on stationery.

Pair the hashtag with a short consent line for guests: ask before posting people, take a photo down if asked, and check with parents before posting children. These come straight from eSafety guidance.

Set expectations that a hashtag gathers posts but doesn't control them: once shared, content can be reshared, and the OAIC notes the Privacy Act doesn't cover individuals posting in a personal capacity. A guest who wants an image removed should first ask the person who posted it.
Guests can manage what they're tagged in through their own settings, so mention this in the welcome pack for anyone who prefers not to be identified.
